 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant- Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 17.02.2011 passed in MVC.No.453/2010 by the Addl. MACT & Fast Track Court-I,
Koppal, questioning the liability fastened on it.

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident and sustaining injuries by the claimant are not disputed.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.
The appellant-Insurance Company has disputed the liability fastened on it on the ground that the driver of lorry was not holding driving licence.
Therefore, submitted that the appellant-Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the lorry.
In the present case, the Tribunal while awarding compensation has fixed the liability on the appellant-Insurance Company.
The owner of lorry is respondent No.3 herein.

The police had conducted the investigation, issued notice under Section 134 (b) of Motor Vehicle Act calling upon respondent No.3 to produce the driving licence and other relevant records, but respondent No.3 has not produced the same.
Respondent No.3, even though, received notice, but has not contested the case.
Respondent No.3 has not produced the driving licence either before the Insurance Company or before the Tribunal or even before this Court in the appeal.
Respondent No.3-owner could have produced the driving licence, but not produced the same.
Therefore, the Insurance Company has discharged its burden in negating that the driver was holding driving licence.
Therefore, it is proved that the driver was not holding driving licence to drive the lorry as on the date of the accident.

Therefore, the appellant-Insurance Company is liable to be NC: 2023:KHC-D:10712 exonerated from payment of compensation, since violation of condition is proved.
Regarding pay and recovery:
6. However, in the present case, the claimant is a third party.

The appellant-Insurance Company has successively established its defence as per Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicle Act and established that the driver of the lorry was not holding driving licence to drive the lorry.

Therefore, as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties and then recover the same from the owner of the lorry bearing No.KA-25/B-6682 as per the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh And Others 1, Pappu And Others Vs. To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

The Insurance Company is at liberty to file execution petition directly before the concerned jurisdictional Court and may seek the order of attachment of movable and immovable properties till recovery of the amount as per law.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following ORDER i.
